newsitem.title: EGYPT: French bank majority shareholder in Egyptian bank.
newsitem.headline: French bank majority shareholder in Egyptian bank.

text.p: Credit Commercial de France (CCF) has become majority shareholder in an Egyptian joint venture after buying a large stake from state-owned National Bank of Egypt (NBE) in a deal worth 26.26 million pounds ($7.7 million), the joint bank said on Tuesday.
NBE sold CCF 11.5 percent of the joint venture, Credit International d'Egypte (CIE), or 82,455 shares at 318.5 pounds a share, CIE chairman Ahmed Shawki said.
After the deal, which was signed in late October, CCF now holds 50.50 percent of CIE.
NBE holds 19.5 percent of CIE, BHF Bank of Germany holds 10 percent and employees of NBE and CIE have the other 20 percent.
The government has embarked on an accelerated privatisation campaign, including the sale of state bank stakes in joint-venture banks.
Under the old regulations, the foreign partners could not own more than 49 percent of the equity in the joint ventures.
Other foreign banks are expected to follow as soon as they can reach agreement with their Egyptian public-sector partners.
